title: Probabilistic trace anchoring and approximate metric contracts
content:
Summary:
This note proposes a lightweight, probabilistic tracing and approximate-metric contract aimed at reducing telemetry volume and query cost for the inference runtime while preserving enough signal for investigations. The approach anchors probabilistic trace sampling to operational triggers (user-visible latency thresholds, kv-cache cold starts, model-fanout) and pairs those samples with compact approximate metrics (count-min sketches, t-digest histograms) surfaced on dashboards.

Goals:
- Reduce trace storage and query costs by ~60% for steady-state traffic without losing signal for high-impact incidents.
- Provide operators deterministic drill paths: when a sampled trace exists, it should contain trace anchors sufficient to reconstruct session context and token-path attribution.
- Offer metric contracts that promise bounded error (relative/absolute) with clear fallbacks to full-resolution telemetry for critical tenants.
- Make dashboards and alerts usable with approximated aggregates and clearly annotate approximation bounds.

Background and motivation:
Token-serving inference produces very high cardinality telemetry: per-request metadata, per-token spans, kv-cache hit vectors, per-tenant model routing. Retaining every trace and raw metric is expensive and noisy. Existing adaptive samplers (severity-weighted, fixed-rate) work well for broad reduction but break deterministic investigation paths: a trace crucial for a regression could be dropped. Anchoring sampling to inexpensive signals ensures we keep more valuable traces.

Key concepts:
- Anchor signals: cheap-to-evaluate binary/quantized indicators computed at ingress or early in the pipeline. Examples: request_latency_bucket, kv_cache_warmth_flag, model_variant_fanout_count, auth_tier. Anchors are evaluated at request time and determine boosted sampling probability.
- Probabilistic anchoring: base sample probability p_base (e.g., 1%) plus additive boost p_anchor for each anchor true for request; clamp to p_max. Anchors have tuned weights to bias for risk and impact.
- Compact trace payloads: sampled traces should include a small set of mandatory spans/attributes: request_id, tenant_id (hashed), model_version, routing_decision, kv_cache_warmth_summary (bitset/summary), latency_by_stage (ingress, compile, first-token, steady-state). Full token-by-token spans are optional and gated by a higher sampling tier.
- Approximate metrics: sketches and t-digest based aggregates replace exact counters/histograms for high-cardinality dimensions. Each metric exposes an error envelope (e.g., 95th percentile +/- 3ms or count error <1%).

Sampling policy (proposal):
- p_base = 0.008 (0.8%) for global sampling of traces.
- Anchors and additive boosts (example):
  - request_latency_bucket == P99: +0.25
  - kv_cache_warmth_flag == COLD: +0.10
  - model_variant_fanout_count > 1: +0.05
  - tenant_is_enterprise: +0.02
- p_max = 0.6 (cap at 60%).
- Emergency override: for incidents flagged by ops (pager or correlation rule) temporarily set p_base = 0.1 and p_max = 1.0 for affected routes.

Sketching and approximate aggregation guidance:
- Use count-min sketches for multi-tenant heavy hitters (top-k token prompts, top source IPs) with explicit hash seeds and width/depth configured per-query-cost targets. Store sketches at 1-min windows and keep raw top-k lists only when heavy-hitter threshold crossed.
- Use t-digest for continuous distributions (latency percentiles). Maintain a rolling t-digest per (route, model_version, tenant_bucket). Expose p50/p90/p95/p99 with uncertainty bounds computed from digest compression parameters.
- For boolean-heavy signals (kv cache warm/cold), keep Bloom filters at short time windows plus a sampled exact counter to calibrate false positive rates.
- Guarantee: approximate count error <= 1% for global counts, relative error bounds for tenant-level counts documented per tenant tier.

Dashboard and alerting patterns:
- Panels must show both the approximated metric line and a shaded band for the approximation envelope; hover text includes the algorithm used and configuration (sketch width, digest compression).
- Operator-facing dashboards: compact view (microdash) for on-call with bolded indicators: approximated p99 latency (with envelope), sampled trace coverage percent, KV cache warm fraction (approx). Drill links should take operator to: sampled-traces view (if available) or to a synthetic probe timeline.
- Alert rules: avoid hard alerts on approximated metrics unless the alert includes a confidence threshold. e.g., alert if p99_approx > 250ms with confidence >= 90% AND sampled_trace_rate >= 0.5% in last 10m.

Trace payload and reconstruction contract:
- A sampled trace must include: request_id (uuid), parent_request_id (if fanout), tenant_bucket (low-entropy hash), route_id, model_version, kv_cache_warmth_summary (8-bit summary), latency_by_stage (ms), sampling_reason_tags (list of anchors that boosted sampling).
- Reconstruction steps for operator: 1) find sample by request_id or time slice; 2) expand anchors to query approximate metrics (via sketches/t-digest) to understand prevalence; 3) if missing token spans, check higher-tier sampling window or trigger on-demand full-capture for the tenant (if SLA allows).

Operator playbook (short):
- High p99 alert: check microdash p99_approx band; verify sampled_trace_coverage > 0.5% in last 5m. If coverage low, escalate to temporary sampling increase or request synthetic run.
- KV cold spike: inspect kv_cache_warmth_summary distribution via Bloom approximation; if heavy-hitter tenants appear, use count-min top-k to list candidate tenant ids (hashed) and request a re-run with debug flags.
- Model rollouts: use anchored sampling to ensure canary traffic has p_anchor +0.4. Validate rollouts by checking per-model t-digest shifts (p95/p99) and sampled trace verdicts for hallucination indicators.

Instrumentation checklist for engineers:
- Emit anchor signals at ingress: request_latency_bucket, kv_cache_warmth_flag, model_variant_fanout_count, tenant_tier. Keep evaluation O(1) and avoid cross-service calls in the hot path.
- Add sampling_reason_tags to trace header when sampled and persist minimal anchor vector to the trace store.
- Publish sketches and t-digest aggregates on 1-min buckets with documented retention policy (30d for sketches, 90d for digest summaries).
- Provide a debug mode per-tenant that can be activated via a short-lived feature flag for full spans capture when investigating an incident.

Rollout plan and measurement:
- Phase 0 (canary): implement anchoring library in a single route with p_base=1% and logs-only recording of sampling decisions for 2 weeks. Compare predicted coverage to observed.
- Phase 1 (service-wide): enable anchoring with default weights; store compact trace payloads and sketches; run both old and new pipelines in parallel for 3 weeks; measure storage and query cost reduction.
- Phase 2 (opt-in tenants): offer tenant-level guarantees and opt-in exact capture for enterprise customers; implement debug mode gating and SLA docs.

Open questions and unknowns:
- Optimal anchor weights per route: need experiments to tune tradeoffs between cost and coverage for regression detection.
- Privacy: hashed tenant identifiers reduce but do not eliminate re-identification risk for small tenants. Need legal review for sketches retention.
- Query UX: how to surface approximate bounds in existing dashboard tooling without overwhelming operators.

Appendix: quick config reference
- Default config (example JSON in prod config store):
  {
    "p_base": 0.008,
    "p_max": 0.6,
    "anchors": {
      "p99_latency": 0.25,
      "kv_cold": 0.1,
      "multi_variant": 0.05,
      "enterprise": 0.02
    },
    "sketches": {
      "width": 4096,
      "depth": 3
    },
    "t_digest_compression": 200
  }

- Related tickets and reading:
  - JIRA OBS-712: implement anchored-sampler library
  - RFC: telemetry-approximation-guardrails (confluence)
  - PR github:infr/telemetry#418: sketch helpers and t-digest wrapper

Notes to self: run small experiments on fanout weight when next inference benchmark run is available. Check SRE oncall feedback after Phase 1 canary.
